items.rationale: Sections 2.4.2 and 7.1.5 cover reinstating the water-damaged panel. The documented area supports the billed 3 m² at about €65/m² for laying, with tiles priced separately.
One pipe penetration was needed to reinstate the panel under §§5.2.6 and 7.1.5. Allow €18 if the drilling is not already included in the laying rate.
Sections 3.5(a) and 7.1.6 limit replacement to the original budget-grade standard. Allow 3 m² at €16/m².
Section 7.1.5 supports levelling material for the roughly 1 m² patch damaged down to brick, not the whole panel. Allow €18 for that patch.

The standard tiles on line 3 already supply the reinstatement; this additional format and quantity are unsupported under §3.5(a), (d) and (e). If accepted instead as a substitute, the allowance would be limited to about €48 for the standard tiles.
Section 7.1.5 limits the allowance to about 3.25 m: 2.4 m at the wall-to-plinth junction and 0.85 m at the side wall. At roughly €11/m, that is €36.

The 12 m premium charge exceeds the documented joints and appears to duplicate line 6, so §3.5(a), (d) and (e) bars it. If separately payable as materials only, allow about €9 for standard sealant for the actual joints.
Section 7.4.2 allows the first necessary travel charge per contractor per document. Allow €70 for the tiler's call-out.

Section 7.4.1 bars separate hours for work already priced in the laying, drilling, jointing and removal lines, and §3.5(b) excludes the attic. If distinct labour for rebuilding the 1 m² patch is substantiated, allow about two hours at €65/hour, not 14 hours.

Section 3.5(c) treats cleaning the reinstated surface as part of the repair, but a routine finishing wipe is included in laying and cannot be charged again under §3.5(d). If a distinct necessary cleaning service is shown, allow about €18.
Sections 2.4.2 and 5.2.6 cover removing the wetted board from the meter boxing. Allow €60 for dismantling only; debris disposal is priced separately.

items.description: Remove and dispose of wet boxing insulation
items.rationale: Section 5.2.1 covers actual removal and disposal. The tiler bagged and took away this wool separately from the container debris, supporting a €45 allowance without duplication.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1.5 support hacking off the damp render across the affected panel, although only 1 m² needed rebuilding down to brick. Allow 3 m² at €24/m² for removal.

Section 3.5(b) excludes work outside the established damage area; the attic staining predates the cellar leak. If the attic work were separately shown to be covered, a small removal job would be about €85.
Section 5.2.6 covers making good after necessary tile removal, during which the old ring cracked. Allow €9 for one ordinary chrome replacement.

Section 2.4.2 expressly includes water escaping from a defective joint. Under §7.1.5, allow about €85 for the limited work of opening the sound fitting, replacing the olive and reassembling it, not replacing the pipe run.

Section 5.2.7 covers one dryer for the week supported by the moisture readings, not precautionary drying after readings returned to normal. Allow seven days at €18/day, inclusive of bundled utilities and ancillary equipment.

Sections 7.4.3–7.4.4 exclude overhead but allow a surcharge tied to necessary repair materials. If itemised as the new olive and sealing paste, rather than amounts already included elsewhere, allow €10.
Sections 2.4.2 and 7.1.6 cover replacing the one metre of sodden lagging with like-for-like rock wool. Allow €22 for the metre, in line with Case 39.
Section 5.2.1 covers the actual small volume of tile, render and plasterboard debris disposed of through the container. Allow €60, excluding the wool the tiler removed separately on line 12.
